• the first systematic map of NLP for
  the whole family (101 codes)

• beyond paper counts: an audit of
  corpora, Wikipedia, morphology,
  LID and parallel data

• conservative wording: 'not found'
  rather than 'does not exist'

• concrete, low-cost priorities, plus a
  companion website and public code
Scope, and where we go next

• we searched indexed venues in English;
  Persian-language journals are a natural
  next addition to the live index

• LLM-assisted screening, checked by people;
  a recall audit of the filter is future work

• the NLP levels summarise resources at a
  glance; a scoring rule would make them
  reproducible

• paper counts show attention, not quality,
  and reflect sanctions and access limits
Computationally Invisible (SilkRoadNLP submission), §3, Limitations, Ethical considerations
